data.body:
`state.scheduled = True` mutates `_ExecutionState` without holding `self._lock`, unlike every other mutation of that object: `_adopt_operations` explicitly locks around `state.operations = dict(operations)` with a comment explaining why a concurrent reader needs a stable rebind, and `_ensure_state`/`_discard_state` also lock.

`on_operation_change` (and `on_invocation_start`/`on_invocation_end`) can run for the same execution ARN from different threads if the SDK dispatches concurrent operation updates (e.g. two branches of a `parallel`/`map` completing around the same time — this is exactly the scenario the existing `_adopt_operations` locking already defends against). Under CPython's GIL a bare `bool` attribute write is not corrupted, so this is currently benign, but it is inconsistent with the class's own locking discipline and is not guaranteed safe on runtimes without a GIL. Guard the write the same way the rest of `_ExecutionState`'s mutations are guarded.
